verses.1: In those days, during the reign of the judges, there was a famine in the land. So, some people from Judah went to live in the fields of Moab, with their wives and two sons.
verses.2: And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife was Naomi. The names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were from the family of Elimelech. They went to Moab’s fields, and they stayed there.
verses.3: And Elimelech, a man of Naaman’s, died. And she and her two sons remained behind.
verses.4: And women from Moab brought them there. One of them died, and the other became pregnant. They stayed there for twelve years.
verses.5: And both of them died from disease and illness. Only the woman remained, along with her two children and her husband.
verses.6: And she and her daughters got up and returned from the fields of Moab. For they heard in the fields of Moab that Jehovah had commanded His people to give them bread.
verses.7: And she went from the place where she had lain down. Her two daughters were with her. She walked along the path back to the land of Judah.
verses.8: And Naomi said to her two daughters, “Go, return to your mother. May the LORD show you kindness, just as He has shown kindness to those who have died.”
verses.9: The LORD will give you peace. A woman will find rest in her husband’s home. He will comfort her, and she will cry out in joy.
verses.10: And we said to her, “You shall return to your people.”
verses.11: And Naomi said, “Return, my daughters. Why should you go with me? I have sons already, and they will be your husbands. They will become your men.”
verses.12: “Behold, my daughters, let us go away, for I am old enough to be a man. For I said, ‘I have a vow on me.’ Also, last night, I was with a man, and I gave birth to children.”
verses.13: May they be fulfilled until they grow taller. They will be bound, and they will not be free. They are not like men at all. I am filled with so much sorrow from them, because it is the hand of Jehovah that has done this to me.
verses.14: And she wept, and continued to cry. She also rubbed her face against her arms, and her tears flowed down.
verses.15: And she said, “Now go back to your people and to your God. I will return after you have gone.”
verses.16: And Ruth said, “Do not abandon me. Do not leave me to go back from your side. For wherever you go, I will go with you. And wherever you stay, I will stay with my people and your God.”
verses.17: When I die, there will be peace. And then I will go to that place. This is what Jehovah will do for me. For death will separate me from you.
verses.18: And it seemed that she was willing to go with him. Then she stopped talking to her.
verses.19: And they walked until they reached the house of bread. When they arrived at the house of bread, all the people in the city gathered around them. They said, “This is what we deserve.”
verses.20: And she said to them, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the LORD has taken away my children.”
verses.21: I am full of sorrow and pain. May Jehovah restore me to my former state. What will you call me, my beloved? And Jehovah answered me, but my enemies were against me.
verses.22: And Naamah and Ruth returned from Moab, along with those who had returned from the fields of Moab. They came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the harvest season.
